title: Does ChatGPT Cite Wikipedia? Yes. Here Is What to Do About It
metaTitle: Does ChatGPT Cite Wikipedia? Should Brands Try? | AEOeye
metaDescription: Yes, ChatGPT cites Wikipedia often. Most brands should not write their own page: Wikipedia's rules block it. Copy the pattern on your own site instead.
shortAnswer: Yes. Wikipedia appears among ChatGPT's most-cited domains in published tests, and Wikimedia says almost all large language models train on it. OpenAI publishes no citation share. Most brands should not write their own page, because Wikipedia needs independent coverage and discourages editing by people with a stake. Copy its pattern on your own site, and add a Wikidata entry only if you meet its criteria.
intro: The short version: ChatGPT leans on Wikipedia, you probably cannot and should not buy your way in, and the useful move is to copy what makes Wikipedia easy to cite. Here is the evidence, then the rules, then what to do instead.

sections.heading: Does ChatGPT cite Wikipedia?
sections.body:
Yes. In the one open study we could check line by line, Wikipedia is among ChatGPT's most-cited domains, though the share varies by query and year. OpenAI publishes no figure, so any single percentage is one study's reading, not a rule.

The best open data point is a September 2025 [University of Toronto preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.08919). Across 50 unbranded cola prompts, a web-search-enabled OpenAI model drew about 19.7% of its citations from Wikipedia. In its car-buying queries, Wikipedia sat among ChatGPT's top domains next to AP News and Reuters. Those were 2025 API models, so treat the numbers as a snapshot.

You will see other shares quoted in vendor studies. We have not verified their methods, so we do not repeat them.

A citation count also misses a second route. When ChatGPT answers from training memory, nothing is cited, so Wikipedia's real influence is larger than any citation share suggests. [How ChatGPT chooses its sources](/answers/how-does-chatgpt-choose-sources) explains the two routes.

One first-hand detail from AEOeye's [crawler access study](/resources/ai-crawler-access-study-2026-10.csv) (fetched 3 October 2026): the robots.txt of en.wikipedia.org did not disallow the homepage for any of the 15 bots we tested, including GPTBot and OAI-SearchBot. The robots.txt of www.reddit.com disallowed all 15. That is one domain each, and homepage-level only, but it shows why Wikipedia is easy for AI systems to reach.

![A library bookshelf lit by sunlight, casting shadows across rows of books](https://images.pexels.com/photos/2946974/pexels-photo-2946974.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=1200)

sections.heading: Why do AI models lean on Wikipedia?
sections.body:
Wikipedia is open to crawlers, enormous, consistently structured and heavily sourced, so it is cheap for a model to learn from and to quote. Three documented facts explain most of the pull.

- **Training.** [Wikimedia says](https://diff.wikimedia.org/2025/10/17/new-user-trends-on-wikipedia/) almost all large language models train on Wikipedia datasets. In the [GPT-3 paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.14165) (2020), Wikipedia was a 3-billion-token dataset, about 0.6% of the tokens in the five datasets by our arithmetic, yet it carried 3% of the training mix and was seen 3.4 times, more than any other source. OpenAI has not published the same detail for current models.
- **Format.** Wikipedia's style guide says a [lead section](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style/Lead_section) should stand on its own as a concise overview: identify the topic, give context, explain why it matters. That is the answer-first pattern.
- **Verifiability.** [Wikipedia's notability rules](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Notability_%28organizations_and_companies%29) state that all content must be verifiable, so claims carry citations a model can follow.

Our inference is that definitional "what is X" questions benefit most, since the first paragraph already answers them.

The flow runs one way. Wikimedia reports human pageviews about 8% below the same months of 2024, and attributes the drop partly to search engines answering directly, often from its content. Answers built on Wikipedia send fewer people back to it.

sections.heading: Should your brand have a Wikipedia page?
sections.body:
Usually not yet, and never one you write yourself. A page survives only if independent sources already cover your company in depth, and nothing we found shows a page makes ChatGPT recommend you.

The independent coverage is the real asset. The Toronto preprint found AI search leans on earned media over brand-owned pages, so the press that would qualify you for a page already feeds AI answers directly. The page is a by-product, not the lever.

Two cautions. A Wikipedia article is written to be neutral, and its lead summarizes prominent controversies too, so you do not control the framing. And if a page exists with errors, ChatGPT may repeat them (our inference), which makes accuracy matter more than presence.

Our position: if you want a page mainly to feel established, you do not have the coverage yet. Spend the effort on earning it. Our guide to [brand mentions](/blog/brand-mentions) explains why independent mentions beat your own pages in AI search.

sections.heading: What are Wikipedia's rules for companies?
sections.body:
Three rules decide whether a company page can exist and who may touch it: notability, conflict of interest and paid-editing disclosure. Each is public and enforced by volunteers.

- **Notability ([WP:NCORP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Notability_%28organizations_and_companies%29)).** A company needs significant coverage in reliable, independent, secondary sources, and several such sources. Press releases, sponsored articles and routine announcements do not count; the guideline says only unpaid sources do. Many trivial sources do not add up to a significant one.
- **Conflict of interest ([WP:COI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Conflict_of_interest)).** Editors with a COI are strongly discouraged from editing affected articles directly. They should disclose it, propose changes on the talk page with the edit COI template, and send new articles through Articles for Creation.
- **Paid editing.** The Wikimedia [Terms of Use](https://foundation.wikimedia.org/wiki/Policy:Terms_of_Use) require anyone paid to contribute to disclose each employer, client, intended beneficiary and affiliation, on a user page, the talk page or in the edit summary.

In practice: if a page about you exists and is wrong, do not fix it yourself. Post a sourced edit request on its talk page and let an uninvolved editor decide.

sections.heading: What should you do instead?
sections.body:
Copy Wikipedia's pattern on your own site, earn the independent coverage that would qualify you, and keep your entity data consistent. Each step helps AI engines whether or not a page ever exists.

1. **Lead with a definition.** Open key pages with a plain statement of what the thing is, as Wikipedia's lead does. See [what makes content quotable by AI](/answers/what-makes-content-quotable-by-ai).
2. **Source every claim** to a primary page, in neutral language. Dated figures, named reports and official documents are what a model can verify and quote; adjectives are not.
3. **One page per question.** On 3 October 2026 we merged 165 of our own pages into 42, because one strong page per question beats five thin ones.
4. **Declare who you are.** Use one brand name everywhere and add Organization schema with `sameAs` links. [Schema.org](https://schema.org/sameAs) defines `sameAs` as a reference page that unambiguously indicates identity, such as a Wikipedia page, Wikidata entry or official website. In our study, 190 of 312 fetched homepages (60.9%) carried schema with `sameAs` links. See [entity SEO](/blog/what-is-entity-seo).
5. **Consider [Wikidata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikidata).** Its [notability bar](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Wikidata:Notability) is lower than Wikipedia's: an item can qualify as a clearly identifiable entity described by serious public references. If you meet it, keep the item accurate and sourced.
6. **Earn mentions** in reviews, comparisons and industry press, the sources that also qualify you for a page.

Then test it. [How ChatGPT chooses its sources](/answers/how-does-chatgpt-choose-sources) shows what is documented. To see who the engines name for your buyers' questions, run AEOeye's [free audit](/): three unbranded buyer questions asked live in ChatGPT, with full answers and the competitors named instead.

keyTakeaways: ChatGPT cites Wikipedia often in published tests (about 19.7% of citations in one 2025 cola experiment), but OpenAI publishes no share.
Wikipedia's pull comes from open access, training weight, a definition-first format and verifiable sourcing.
Most brands should not write their own page: WP:NCORP needs independent coverage and WP:COI discourages direct editing.
The independent coverage that earns a page also feeds AI answers directly, so earn that first.
Copy the pattern on your own site and keep entity data consistent, with Wikidata if you qualify.

faqs.q: How often does ChatGPT cite Wikipedia?
faqs.a: OpenAI publishes no figure. In one 2025 University of Toronto experiment with 50 unbranded cola prompts, a web-search-enabled OpenAI model took about 19.7% of its citations from Wikipedia. Shares differ by query type, model version and year, so treat any single percentage as a snapshot of one study rather than a rule.

faqs.q: Do I need a Wikipedia page to show up in ChatGPT?
faqs.a: No. We found no OpenAI documentation or study showing that a page is required or that it guarantees a recommendation. What matters more is independent coverage, clear definition-first pages on your own site and consistent entity signals. A Wikipedia page, if you qualify, is a by-product of that coverage rather than a prerequisite.

faqs.q: Can I edit Wikipedia to add my company?
faqs.a: You can, but you should not do it directly. Wikipedia strongly discourages editing by people with a conflict of interest, and paid contributors must disclose their employer, client and affiliation under the Wikimedia Terms of Use. Propose changes on the talk page with an edit request, or submit a draft through Articles for Creation.

faqs.q: Is a Wikidata entry worth creating for my brand?
faqs.a: Only if you meet its criteria: a clearly identifiable entity that can be described using serious, publicly available references, or one that has a Wikimedia sitelink or serves a structural need. If you qualify, an accurate, sourced item can anchor your sameAs links. If you do not qualify, spend the time on independent coverage and consistent schema instead.

definitions.definition: Wikimedia's free, structured knowledge base. Each entity is an item with sourced statements and identifiers, separate from Wikipedia's articles.
Wikipedia's notability guideline for organizations and companies: significant coverage in several reliable, independent, secondary sources; press releases and sponsored content do not count.

On Wikipedia, a situation where an editor's connection to a subject, such as employment or payment, may compromise neutrality. Such editors are strongly discouraged from editing the affected article directly.
